title: Nano cross-process idempotency battery @ agent-passport-gateway 99888e8 — pre-registered R1/R2a/R2b/R3/R4 + invariant (PR #14)

subject.sut_note: The vendor's actual implementation at the pin, executed in TWO INDEPENDENT OS PROCESSES per trial against one file-backed SQLite database (WAL, busy_timeout 5000) — not a re-implementation. Offline: no network, no real Nano publishing; the fake Nano node mirrors the vendor's own test harness (test/payment-rails/nano-publish.test.ts) and records every call. Deterministic scheduling via file barriers: sequenced trials fix the interleave; sim trials release both processes together and record the observed winner (assertions order-agnostic). Runner: sut-nano-cross-process-battery/run-battery.mjs + worker.ts (sha256 in layer1-log meta). The battery observes WalletOpError codes and applies the pinned route mapping (wallet-routes.ts:142-144: bad_request→400, else→409) for the registered 409 expectations; the HTTP route layer itself is not booted. Pinned vendor files sha256 at the pin: wallet-ops.ts 5efcba3d…, nano-publish.ts ac80f093…, wallet-routes.ts f6e55b17…, wallet-frontier.ts 69dc1916…, nano-block.ts dd5ad69a…, schema.ts 3f63330b… (full values in layer1-gate.md). Vendor's own wallet-ops suite passes 22/22 at the pin in this environment before the battery was built.
subject.lab_run_branch: main (public proof-layer registry; evidence hash-pinned in this record)
subject.pre_registration: Pre-registered in x402-foundation/x402 issue #4198, comment 6817874244 (igor-vii): SUT agent-passport-gateway @ 99888e8, two OS processes on one file-backed SQLite, fake Nano node from the PR test harness, rows R1-R4 + invariant frozen as of the post. SUT owner aeoess (Tymofii Pidlisnyi) asked the single pre-run question (comment 6829861656): R2's starting state; resolved BEFORE the first artifact by the amendment (comment 6831739390): R2 split into R2a (key already exists → both changed requests 409, zero new reservations, stored operation byte-identical) and R2b (key new → exactly one reservation, loser 409, budget decremented once by the winner only). Original R2 and the split are both shown in this record — nothing re-interpreted after the fact. Pin discipline honored: PR #14 merged into main as 4784153 but the battery ran against the registered pin 99888e8 only, which IS an ancestor of main (plain checkout; the fact is recorded). This pre-registration contains no 24-hour hold clause (unlike the wave-2 registration); the owner separately welcomed the run regardless of outcome. No registered row was added, removed or re-interpreted at any point.

findings_summary.title: Pin acquisition: commit 99888e8 dated 2026-11-11 22:18:15 -0800 (= 2026-11-12T06:18:15Z), an ancestor of current main (PR #14 merged as 4784153) — plain clone+checkout, no fetch-by-SHA. All validation and the battery ran on the pinned checkout only, per the owner's explicit request.

Layer-1 gate passed before the first artifact: all thread quotes verified verbatim at the pin (S1-S8, layer1-gate.md) — reserveSend single .immediate() transaction with key+budgets+inserts, replayOrMismatch fingerprint semantics, refuseIfAccountBusy wallet_busy, 409 route mapping, commitAttempt/publishAttempt one-token stored-block semantics (vendor's own C3 pins retry-identical-block), takeOver claim fencing, WAL/busy_timeout substrate. Ten pinned files hash-pinned. Vendor's own wallet-ops suite: 22/22 PASS at the pin in this environment before the battery was built.

Harness iterations disclosed: an infrastructure smoke trial (distinct key, not a registered row) and one full-battery iteration exposed three harness defects (missing dbFile param; fixture delegation chain not linked so the budget decremented one hop only; R4 role-A control-flow fall-through into the retry branch). All three are battery-harness bugs, not SUT divergences; no registered expectation was altered to accommodate them. The sealed verdicts are from the corrected runner; observed SUT behavior was identical across iterations.

Scope facts: the battery drives the vendor's real code cross-process; sim trials observe a true simultaneous race (winner recorded, assertions order-agnostic), sequenced trials fix the interleave. The fake Nano node records every call (account_info/work_generate/process) — signature count is observable through the node log since prepareOp is the only signing path. No HTTP routes booted: 409 expectations verified at the WalletOpError layer with the pinned route mapping cited. No defect claim — all registered rows PASS on the pinned implementation.

notes: Battery result: 12 trials + invariant = 13/13 rows PASS, 106/106 checks, zero divergences (verdicts.md). R1 (both orderings + simultaneous): exactly one reservation wins in every ordering; the loser observes the original operation (replay: true, same op id) without reserving or signing again; delegation budget decremented exactly once (1000 raw on both hops of the two-hop chain in every trial); the winner alone prepares (one account_info, one work_generate), commits and publishes once — exactly one process call, and the published block is byte-identical to the stored block_json. R2a (pre-existing key, both processes race with changed amount/recipient): both receive idempotency_mismatch (= 409 under the pinned route mapping); zero new reservations (the pre-op's holds only); the stored operation row is byte-identical after the race; budget untouched; zero node calls. R2b (fresh key, different amounts 1000 vs 2000, both orderings + simultaneous): exactly one reservation — the first writer under BEGIN IMMEDIATE commits, the loser receives idempotency_mismatch (409) against the winner's stored fingerprint; budget decremented exactly once, by the winner only (1000 on both hops when A wins, 2000 on both hops when B wins). R3 (different keys, same wallet, first payment unfinished, both orderings + simultaneous): the second operation is refused with wallet_busy (409); exactly one wallet_ops row, status reserved (unfinished); neither process signs — zero node calls at all; budget decremented once. R4 (retry after publication, across processes): process A reserves, prepares the one block, commits and publishes (accepted); process B retries the same key and payment, receives the original operation (replay: true, same op id, status admitted), never calls prepareOp — B's node log contains exactly one action: process; B takes over the expired lease, commits one more attempt and publishes the SAME stored block — the two process calls are byte-identical and both match the stored block_json; attempt history [1: accepted, 2: accepted]; attempt_count = 2; one operation, one reservation, budget decremented once. Invariant: reservation count == 1 in every R1 trial (distinct reserved op ids, one set of holds); no budget underflow (spend_used_minor <= spend_limit_minor on every delegation in every trial); no double-reserve anywhere.
